BM25 yields a recall of 80.8%, and dense retrieval yields 95.6%. We use the provided entity descriptions. Table 2 shows that, for the accuracy on actual entities, LELA performs on par with the classical approaches. In the overall accuracy, the baseline that always predicts UNK has the highest accuracy, which is due to the high ratio of UNK mentions. LELA still outperforms the other true zero-shot competitors, as well as the classical approaches. Dense retrieval of candidates allows for higher non- UNK accuracy across the models, while BM25 results in higher UNK accuracy, and thus in higher general accuracy given the high UNK proportion, but overall, the choice of the retrieval method does not lead to statistically significant differences in accuracy. GLADIS Chen et al. ( 2023 ) is a benchmark for the task of mapping acronyms to their inferred long form, spanning three domains: the general, scientific and the biomedical domain, with, respectively, 7125, 14066 and 2909 test mentions. The average number of candidates per acronym is 200. We use the short-form to long-form mapping for candidate generation, and use the long-forms as entity descriptions. Classical entity linking approaches have not been applied to the acronym disambiguation task.
